# `supabase/security-definer-view`: View bypasses Row Level Security

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family   | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                    |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| supabase | medium           | 5.5                      | [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html), [CWE-269](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

Views in exposed schemas that run with their owner's privileges, that is, created without
`WITH (security_invoker = true)` (Postgres 15+) and not later altered to set it. RLS on the
underlying tables is then not applied to the caller. Reported at **medium** severity and
medium confidence.

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

By default a Postgres view runs with the privileges of its owner (usually postgres), so RLS on the underlying tables is not applied to the caller. A view in an exposed schema can therefore leak rows that the tables themselves protect, including rows from auth.users.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- View {view} runs with its owner's privileges (no security_invoker), so Row Level Security of the tables it reads is bypassed.

## How to fix

Create the view WITH (security_invoker = true) (Postgres 15+) so the caller's RLS applies, or move it to a non-exposed schema.

### Vulnerable

```sql
create view public.user_emails as
  select id, email from auth.users;
```

### Fixed

```sql
create view public.my_profile
  with (security_invoker = true) as
  select id, full_name from public.profiles;
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Views over public data** (for example a view of published posts) leak nothing. Add
  `security_invoker = true` anyway, or suppress with the reason.
- **Views with API privileges revoked** (`REVOKE ALL ON … FROM anon, authenticated`) are
  still reported in v1. If you revoked them on purpose, suppress with that reason.
- **Limitations:** VibeGuard does not check which tables the view reads, so it cannot tell
  whether rows are actually exposed. Materialized views are not analysed.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```sql
-- vibeguard-ignore-next-line supabase/security-definer-view -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the statement VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  supabase/security-definer-view: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html): Improper Access Control
- [CWE-269](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html): Improper Privilege Management
